item.title: Mediating gates between polar molecules using microwave-dressed Rydberg atoms
item.description:
Pay dirt theory — Microwave-dressed Rydberg 133Cs atoms mediate an entangling modified iSWAP gate between 23Na133Cs molecules in tG=0.37 μs at rRm=1 μs, with estimated infidelity 1−ℱ∼10−2.

Grade 0.474 · 2.5σ above the day's baseline · matched “Quantum information with Rydberg atoms” · Bas Gerritsen, Sean R. Muleady, Arghavan Safavi-Naini, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Jeremy T. Young

Figure

Gate infidelity and optimal atom-molecule spacing plotted against thermal excitation n‾x and spacing rRm, comparing total infidelity with post-selection.

Asks

How to execute fast, parallel entangling gates between polar molecules while suppressing unwanted inter-mediator interactions?

Before

was tGiSWAP≈230 μs for direct molecule-molecule interaction at rmm=1 μs

But

Off-resonant weak molecular dressing limit, theoretical simulation of leading-order 1D motional and decay infidelities, atom tweezer switched off during gate.

Tools

Microwave dressing of Rydberg states · Quantized 1D motional wave-packet model · Modified iSWAP gate mediation · Erasure detection by atomic readout

Abstract

We propose a scheme for mediating many simultaneous, fast entangling gates between pairs of polar molecules using Rydberg atoms. By using microwave drives, the dipolar interactions between Rydberg atoms are nullified. Using the freedom left in the microwave dressing parameters, the Rydberg van der Waals interactions are minimized and the Rydberg-molecule interaction is tuned into resonance, allowing for the mediation of a modified iSWAP gate between molecules. In the example of mediating gates between ²³Na ¹³³Cs molecules with ¹³³Cs atoms, the gate is more than two orders of magnitude faster than an equivalent direct molecule-molecule gate. We model the decay of the dressed Rydberg states and the motion of the atom and molecules and obtain a leading-order estimate of the resulting gate infidelities. Finally, we show that by detecting the state of the Rydberg atom after a gate, a subset of gate errors can be converted into erasure errors and mitigated by post-selection or quantum error-correction.

item.title: Fundamental Physics at the Frontier of Noisy Quantum Computation
item.description:
Pay dirt review — Presents scalable variational algorithms and error-mitigated/error-detected frameworks on up to 120 qubits, giving numerical evidence for inelastic particle production in scalar field theory and exceeding unencoded local observable estimation by >200% at late times using [[4,2,2]] encoded circuits in 2D Ising simulations.

Grade 0.437 · 2.1σ above the day's baseline · matched “Probing many-body dynamics on a 51-atom quantum simulator” · Nikita A. Zemlevskiy

Asks

How can quantum simulation algorithms, error management strategies, and quantum-information tools be co-designed to simulate fundamental quantum field theory dynamics and scattering processes on noisy-to-partially-fault-tolerant quantum processors?

But

Ancilla leakage and lack of fast resets cause effective inter-block coupling slowdown Jeff=J(1−2pflip); higher syndrome measurement rounds inject coherence-time noise that can outweigh error detection.

Tools

SC-ADAPT-VQE · Scalable Variational Circuits (SVC) · [[4,2,2]] quantum error-detecting code · IBM superconducting quantum processors · Matrix Product State (MPS) simulations

Abstract

Quantum computing offers a new, orthogonal direction for investigating fundamental physics, extending beyond classical numerical methods and conventional observables. Realizing this potential requires directly confronting the noise limiting currently available quantum computers. Progress rests on advancing algorithms, interpreting their results, and managing their errors together. This thesis presents several advancements in the use of quantum simulation and quantum information to probe fundamental physics. The first is in the use of quantum computers to simulate collisions in quantum field theories. Central to these simulations are new wavepacket preparation, time evolution, and error mitigation techniques, which allow for simulations with some of the largest effective circuit volumes to date. These methods enable the first quantum simulation providing numerical evidence for inelastic particle production, a key process in fundamental physics. The second advancement centers on the role quantum-information-theoretic quantities play in physical processes. Beyond mere correlations with the physics of the process, entanglement and magic are shown to probe the interactions present in scattering and hadronization dynamics. A precision study requires a complete quantification of algorithmic and hardware uncertainties, an outstanding goal as quantum simulations mature. The third advancement in this thesis addresses error management. A framework minimizing the effect of algorithmic errors in analog quantum simulations is presented. In a step toward fault tolerance, error detection in encoded quantum simulations is shown to improve estimation of local observables relative to unencoded runs. Together, the developments in this thesis mark practical progress toward fault-tolerant quantum simulations of fundamental physics capable of scientific discovery.

item.title: Optical quantum cascade laser based on a MIM structure
item.description:
Worth a look theory — Theoretical demonstration of a quantum cascade laser using diamond-metal MIM heterostructures capable of spanning UV to THz radiation ranges via metastable quantum well levels.

Grade 0.411 · 1.8σ above the day's baseline · matched “cavity QED, atom-photon interfaces and quantum networks” · Michael V. Davidovich

Asks

Can metal-insulator-metal (MIM) heterostructures based on diamond and metal films support optical quantum cascade lasing across wide frequency bands?

But

Theoretical calculation only.

Tools

metal-insulator-metal (MIM) heterostructures · diamond and metal thin films · quantum potential profiling · metastable level modeling

Abstract

A quantum cascade laser based on a metal-insulator-metal structure is proposed, the heterostructure of which consists of diamond and metal films. The profile of the quantum potential in a quasi-periodic MIM heterostructure and the structure of metastable levels in quantum wells are investigated. A number of CCL configurations have been proposed. The possibility of generating radiation from the UV to THz range is theoretically shown.

item.title: 100 million photons per second from a single organic molecule
item.description:
Worth a look new result — Cryogenic planar metallo-dielectric antenna achieves 97% first-lens collection efficiency and collects 108 photons per second into a 0.77NA lens from a single DBT molecule. Emitted photons exhibit single-photon purity g(2)(0)<2.5% and (91.2±2.3)% indistinguishability.

Grade 0.389 · 1.5σ above the day's baseline · matched “Quantum information with Rydberg atoms” · Siwei Luo, Tim Hebenstreit, Alexey Shkarin, Jan Renger, Tobias Utikal, Stephan Goetzinger

Figure

Back focal plane emission profile within the 0.77NA acceptance angle and time-resolved fluorescence decay confirming directional photon collection.

Asks

Can photon extraction from single organic molecules be engineered to achieve cryogenic single-photon generation rates comparable to solid-state quantum emitters without damaging organic host crystals?

Before

Previous cryogenic single-molecule sources reached detected count rates an order of magnitude lower.

But

Measured at approximately 1.4K; indistinguishability is limited by residual pure dephasing.

Tools

planar metallo-dielectric antenna · hemispherical ZrO₂ solid immersion lens · DBT:p-DCB organic crystal nanochannel · Hong-Ou-Mandel fibre interferometer · Hanbury Brown-Twiss APD setup

Abstract

At cryogenic temperatures, organic single-photon sources (SPSs) offer Fourier-limited emission, virtually unlimited photostability, and emission wavelengths selectable by molecular design, making them attractive for quantum metrology, secure communication, and photonic quantum information processing. However, their efficient integration with photonic microstructures has remained challenging, limiting photon collection from single organic emitters under cryogenic operation. Here, we demonstrate a cryogenic planar metallo-dielectric antenna that efficiently directs the emission of a single dibenzoterrylene (DBT) molecule towards the collection optics. The device reaches a collection efficiency of 97% and delivers 100 million photons per second into the first lens. We measure a photon indistinguishability for the Fourier-limited transition of 91.2% while maintaining a high single-photon purity of 97.7% under strong continuous-wave (CW) and pulsed excitation. These results establish organic molecules as a high-performance platform for single-photon generation and represent an important step towards scalable organic quantum photonic technologies.
